correctness.rationale: PO is equivalent to assigning each good to an approver: otherwise transfer to an approver gives Pareto improvement; supported allocations maximize sum utility. Under binary values and supported assignments, EQX is exactly max_i u_i-min_i u_i<=1, which implies EFX by removing an approved good from any holder’s bundle. Because each agent approves two goods, utilities are 0,1,2; the range condition implies a matching saturates either all agents (u>=1) or all goods (u<=1), and such matchings construct the allocation. Edge-to-vertex injections exist in a connected multigraph iff e<=v (tree/unicyclic orientations); vertex-to-edge injections iff e>=v (spanning unicyclic subgraph). Thus mixed e<v and e>v components are the sole obstruction. Lower bounds four multigraph agents and six simple-edge agents follow from minimum multicyclic component edge count plus separate tree; explicit witnesses attain them. Independent enumerator tested all 1296 ordered four-edge profiles using four goods against all supported allocations.

final_claim: For all finite 0/1-goods instances with exactly two approved goods per agent and each good approved, complete PO+EFX+EQX allocation exists iff the approval multigraph has no tree component together with a distinct multicyclic component; equivalently the agent-good incidence graph has a matching saturating its smaller bipartition.
limitations: Additive binary values, each agent exactly two distinct approved goods, every good approved; no claim without PO.
Independent enumeration tests 1296 labeled small profiles; all-size proof is matching and multigraph structure.
